scenes.label: YALE, BEINECKE MS 408
lines: This book is about six hundred years old.
And nobody alive can read a single word of it.

scenes.label: THE VOYNICH MANUSCRIPT
lines: About two hundred and forty pages of an unknown script, strange plants and star charts.

scenes.label: FIVE SCRIBES
lines: A 2020 handwriting study found five different scribes wrote it.
Every claimed translation so far has fallen apart.

scenes.label: THE TWIST
lines: Then, in 2025, a researcher showed that a medieval-style cipher using dice and playing cards can turn Latin into text that looks just like it.
It doesn't crack the code. But it means the book may not be nonsense.
Follow for one mystery every day.

youtube.description:
A book about 600 years old that nobody can read. The Voynich manuscript (Yale, Beinecke MS 408) has about 240 pages of an unknown script, strange plants and star charts. Radiocarbon dating in 2009 put its vellum between 1404 and 1438, and a 2020 study found five scribes wrote it. In 2025 a published study showed a cipher using dice and playing cards can produce text with the same patterns. It does not solve the mystery, but it suggests the book may not be gibberish.
